hints.title: Correlating Playbacks with Advertising
hints.text: Join each streaming session with ads shown to that customer falling within the session time frame.

hints.title: Temporal Window Condition
hints.text: Match on identical customer_id where the ad timestamp is between the session start_time and end_time.

hints.title: Isolating Sessions Without Interruptions
hints.text: Perform a left join and filter for records where the matched ad identifier is null.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p.session_id
FROM Playback p
LEFT JOIN Ads a ON p.customer_id = a.customer_id
  AND a.timestamp BETWEEN p.start_time AND p.end_time
WHERE a.ad_id IS NULL;
```

complexity.time: O(P + A) with index on Ads(customer_id, timestamp)
complexity.notes: Anti-join pattern using LEFT JOIN and IS NULL on timestamp range.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: NOT IN subqueries fail or degrade if null values appear in the correlated ad tables.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Range index on timestamp speeds up the between evaluation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should apply standard anti-join syntax with proper timestamp range filtering.

import pandas as pd

def ad_free_sessions(playback: pd.DataFrame, ads: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = playback.merge(ads, on="customer_id", how="left")
    interrupted = merged[(merged["timestamp"] >= merged["start_time"]) & (merged["timestamp"] <= merged["end_time"])]["session_id"].unique()
    res = playback[~playback["session_id"].isin(interrupted)][["session_id"]]
    return res
